OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: "(?s).*\\S.*"
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: "(?s).*\\S.*"
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create/update it is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a
            leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise country
            code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+', and
            that E.164 string is the stored/returned value (e.g. '0412 345 678'
            becomes '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address. It is normalized to lower-case, and the
            stored/returned value is that lower-cased string.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; when omitted
            it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even if another owner already
            has the same last name and address (i.e. they share a household).
            Optional; defaults to false.
          type: boolean
          example: false

The full test suite is green: **262 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors**.

## Summary

Implemented rejection of a supplied `registrationDate` later than the server date with a 400 response.

**Change** — `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (`src/main/java/.../v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`):

```java
if (ownerFieldsDto.getRegistrationDate() != null
    && ownerFieldsDto.getRegistrationDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now())) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);
}
```

This runs before the existing default-to-`LocalDate.now()` logic. It only rejects an *explicitly supplied* future date; a `null` registrationDate still defaults to the server's current date, and today's date is accepted (`isAfter` is strict).

**Tests added** (`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.java`):
- `createOwnerRejectedWhenRegistrationDateInFuture` — tomorrow's date → 400.
- `createOwnerAllowedWhenRegistrationDateToday` — today's date → 201, confirming the boundary isn't over-rejected.

I placed the guard in the create path only, matching the spec (registration date is a create-time field — `updateOwner` never touches `registrationDate`).
